title: Digitized EKG
description: One EKG photo turned into numbers. Times are in milliseconds (ms) from the start of the strip. Amplitudes are in millivolts (mV). Positive amplitude points up on the paper. 0 mV is the baseline.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file was written for. No unit. Must match the version of this schema file exactly. The number goes up on every field change.

image_id.description: ID of the source photo this data came from. No unit. Must not contain patient information.

calibration.description: How pixels in the photo were turned into time and voltage.

mm_per_s.description: Paper speed in millimeters per second (mm/s). Standard EKG paper is 25.

mm_per_mv.description: Gain in millimeters per millivolt (mm/mV). Standard EKG paper is 10.

px_per_mm.description: Image pixels per millimeter of grid paper (px/mm).

source.description: Where the calibration values came from. No unit. default = standard paper values were assumed. detected = measured from the grid in the photo. manual = entered by a person.

sample_rate_hz.description: Samples per second, in hertz (Hz). The same for every lead. The time of sample i in a lead is start_ms + i * 1000 / sample_rate_hz. This is the time axis, so no time array is stored.

leads.description: The digitized leads. Any of the 12 standard leads may be present. None is required on its own, but there must be at least one.

overall_confidence.description: Confidence in the whole result. No unit. 0 = no confidence, 1 = full confidence.

flags.description: Problems found in the photo. No unit. Empty array when no problem was found.

start_ms.description: Time of the first sample of this lead, in milliseconds (ms) from the start of the strip.

amplitude_mv.description: The signal, one number per sample, in millivolts (mV). Positive values point up. 0 is the baseline. Samples are evenly spaced at sample_rate_hz.

confidence.description: Confidence in this lead's signal. No unit. 0 = no confidence, 1 = full confidence.

beats.description: Heartbeats found in this lead, in time order. Empty array when wave boundaries have not been detected.

beat.description: One heartbeat. All three keys must be present. Use null for p or t when that wave is missing.

p.description: P wave, or null when no P wave exists.

qrs.description: QRS complex. Its peak is the R peak. Never null, because a beat is found by its QRS.

t.description: T wave, or null when no T wave was found.

wave.description: Boundaries of one wave. Order must be onset, then peak, then offset. JSON Schema cannot check that order; the checkWaveOrder helper does.

onset_ms.description: Where the wave starts, in milliseconds (ms) from the start of the strip.

peak_ms.description: Where the wave is furthest from the baseline, in milliseconds (ms) from the start of the strip.

offset_ms.description: Where the wave ends, in milliseconds (ms) from the start of the strip.

amplitude_mv.description: Signal value at the peak, in millivolts (mV). Positive points up. Negative for a wave that points down.
